rubric.name: Communication
rubric.next: Open with the answer in one sentence, name the sections you will cover, and say when you move on.
levels: Hard to follow
Ideas arrive in no order
Understandable, with some rambling
Clear order, signposted, concise
Clear, concise, and the follow-up gets a direct answer

rubric.name: Product vision
rubric.next: After the diagnosis or the design, say what you would build next and the user outcome it serves.
levels: No view of where the product should go
Fixes the symptom only
Names a better experience for one user
Ties the solution to a clear user outcome
Ties the solution to a product direction and says what you would not build

rubric.name: Prioritization
rubric.next: Rank the options on impact and effort, pick one first, and give the reason in one line.
levels: No choices made
Lists options without ranking
Picks one and gives no reason
Picks one and ranks the rest by impact and effort
Picks one, weighs the cost, and says what waits and why

rubric.name: Business strategy
rubric.next: Link the answer to the company goal, then name one trade-off, such as engagement against revenue.
levels: The business is never mentioned
Mentions revenue or growth in passing
Links the answer to one company goal
Links to the goal and names one trade-off
Links to the goal, weighs the trade-offs, and says what you would watch for

rubric.name: Data literacy
rubric.next: Name the metric you would check first, the segment you would cut it by, and what result would change your mind.
levels: No metrics named
Names a metric with no reason
Picks relevant metrics
Picks metrics, segments them, and says what each would show
Picks metrics, segments them, names a counter-metric, and says what would change your mind

Product Design: Which user would you cut from your scope, and why?
What is the biggest risk to your idea, and how would you test it?
Your engineering lead says it takes three times longer. What do you cut?
How would you know in four weeks that it is working?
Analytics: What would make you doubt this number?
Which segment would you look at first, and why?
What would you do if two metrics moved in opposite directions?
How big a change would you need to see before you acted?
Strategy: What would make you change your mind?
Who loses if you do this?
What is the cheapest test of your main assumption?
What would you choose not to build?
Technical: What breaks first when traffic grows ten times?
What would you ask the engineers before committing?
What does the user see if this fails?
Which part could degrade without hurting the user?
Behavioral: What did you personally do, as opposed to the team?
What would you do differently now?
How did you know it worked?
What was the hardest disagreement, and how did it end?
General: What would you do in the first week?
Who would you talk to first?
What is the common mistake here?

bands.label: Early
bands.line: Keep going with fundamentals. Do the lessons, then repeat this with shorter questions.

bands.label: Developing
bands.line: You have the shape of an answer. Work on the weakest criterion below.

bands.label: Getting ready
bands.line: Solid on most criteria. Repeat under tighter time and with harder questions.

bands.label: Strong on this evidence
bands.line: Your own ratings are high. Check them with a friend who will be honest.
